claims.statement: The Agentic OS Console is a Next.js 15 App Router application (package @harness/console) inside the repository's Bun workspace (apps/*), started from the repo root via bun run console; its runtime dependencies are limited to next/react/zustand, react-markdown/remark-gfm, and lucide-react, and server code uses only node:* builtins (child_process, fs, os, path) - no new server runtime dependencies.

The console is layered as pages/components/zustand store → fetch (RSC payload / JSON / SSE) → API routes (src/app/api) → src/core modules → src/runtimes adapters → machine touchpoints (filesystem reads, ps snapshot + signals, headless agent CLIs); API routes build a ServerContext (repoRoot + loaded state + ADAPTERS + saveState) via src/lib/server-context.ts rather than touching the FS or spawning directly, and adapters receive a ProbeContext (repoRoot, home, workspaces, FsSignalHelpers) so they never access the filesystem directly.

The source of truth for the runtime list is .agents/runtime/<vendor>/config.json on disk: loadVendorConfigs() scans that directory and skips folders without a valid config.json, and a new harness vendor appears on the dashboard automatically; the UI never hardcodes runtime lists because GET /api/runtimes/list feeds the client store and src/plugins/runtimes/ supplies only cosmetic monogram/color styling.

Live runtime behavior is provided by optional RuntimeAdapter implementations in src/runtimes/<id>.ts (claude, codex, zcode, cursor, kimi, opencode) registered at the single ADAPTERS point in src/runtimes/index.ts; without an adapter a card still renders from the vendor config with status unknown, and a throwing adapter sets probeError but never crashes the dashboard probe.

probeRuntimes() merges adapter signals, ps process scan, shared + adapter diagnostics, and awaiting-input heuristics, then classifies activity with the pure classifyActivity() (active-now ≤ 5 minutes, recently-active within the selected window, inactive beyond, disabled when isInstalled is false); probes run in parallel and accept only: [id] so the /runtime/[id] space page probes one runtime instead of all six.

Console state persists in .agents/console/state.json (outside Git, overridable via HARNESS_CONSOLE_STATE): it holds the MCP registry, skill overlays (useGlobal/defaults/runtimeOverrides), defaultRuntime, taskRuntimes, plugins, workspaces with openwiki/graphify/docs subsets, installed tools, and lastMcpSync results; loadConsoleState merges onto defaults so a missing or corrupt file starts the console with defaults, and saveConsoleState writes atomically via state.json.tmp + rename.

Every mutating API route follows the chain: mutate state → await saveState() → respond → client store updates only after server confirmation → invalidateDashboardCache(); the zustand store (src/store/console.ts) mirrors this by calling set() only after a successful PATCH/PUT, so the client store never leads the file, and only UI preferences (windowKey, autoRefresh) are persisted to localStorage via partialize.

The dashboard micro-cache (src/core/cache.ts) applies a 5-second TTL plus inflight dedup of concurrent recomputes keyed by repoRoot|window, is shared by the RSC page (src/app/page.tsx) and GET /api/runtimes, and is cleared via invalidateDashboardCache() by all mutating routes (mcp, plugins, runtimes, settings, skills, skills-sh/install, tools/action, tools/dashboard, workspaces).

Process handling uses a single cached ps snapshot per probe cycle (2 s TTL in src/lib/signals/processes.ts); before any signal, stopProcess/restartProcess re-verify the PID with a fresh (cache-bypassing) ps slice against the runtime's processPattern, stop escalates SIGTERM → up to 3 s grace → SIGKILL, and restart is limited to macOS .app bundles via open -a.

The API surface is a registry of force-dynamic routes under src/app/api/**/route.ts covering runtimes, mcp (+catalog), skills (+installed/create/remove), skills-sh (search/detail/install/SSE/input), plugins (+marketplace), processes (+action), sessions (+reply), prompts/run, settings, tools (action/diagnose/dashboard/job SSE/usage), workspaces (+clone), memory (docs/openwiki/graphify/runtimes/file/visualizer/llm), plus the GET /dashboard/* Headroom embed proxy with literal upstream http://127.0.0.1:8787/dashboard.

Long-running installs stream to the UI as SSE jobs: skills-sh installs use the in-memory job manager (core/installJobs.ts) while tool jobs (core/toolJobs.ts) duplicate output into file logs (.agents/console/tool-jobs/jobs.log + jobs-meta.jsonl with id-tab-prefixed lines) that the SSE route polls, making the stream invariant to Next.js HMR and per-route module copies; jobId is used only as a line-prefix filter, never in file paths.

All process spawns use literal commands (bunx, claude, codex, kimi, opencode, node, open, sh) with argument arrays and no shell; prompts are sanitized (NUL stripped, 32 kB cap, leading-dash disarmed), MCP and skill-package names pass strict regexes, and wrapper functions around spawn are deliberately avoided because the Mimosa pre-commit scanner would block them - the accepted pattern is an inline switch over literals.

Server-side outbound requests are SSRF-guarded: skill metadata fetches allow only http/https to skills.sh/github.com/deepwiki.com with private-range rejection, timeouts, and response caps; git clone accepts only https URLs whose host is not localhost/private and confines the target directory inside sources/.

GET /api/memory/file reads files only through checkReadPath()'s allowlist policy: markdown files inside workspace roots, non-hidden files inside <dir>/openwiki/ and runtime memory directories, and single global files (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), enforced by lexical path equality, realpath containment (symlink escape rejected), hidden-component rejection, and a size cap.

MCP sync gives each target ownership of exactly the names from the console registry minus what it wrote last sync - foreign entries in runtime config files are never touched; the project .mcp.json receives globally enabled servers while per-runtime user configs apply final = runtimeOverride ?? enabled, and the Codex target is edited by the sectional TOML editor in src/lib/toml.ts.

Session replies and prompt runs are headless CLI integrations driven by adapter replyCommand/runCommand: POST /api/sessions/reply spawns resume commands (claude -p --resume, codex exec resume, ...) with a 120 s timeout and capped output, while POST /api/prompts/run and buildFixPrompt launch new detached sessions whose output goes to .agents/console/runs/<ts>-<runtime>.log.

Extension points: adding a runtime requires (1) .agents/runtime/<id>/config.json, (2) a src/runtimes/<id>.ts adapter plus one ADAPTERS line, and (3) an optional src/plugins/runtimes/<id>.ts UI plugin; adding a context-saving tool means registering a ToolDef in src/core/tools.ts plus same-commit updates to tooling/scripts/tool.sh, setup.sh, and docs/tools.md - TOOL_RUNTIMES in core/tools.ts is the deliberate documented exception to the no-hardcoded-runtime-lists rule.

Focused bun test suites cover the architecture's core contracts with pure functions and fixtures: activity classification boundaries, vendor-config discovery and probe DTO behavior (adapter-less → unknown, broken configs skipped), state load-merge/atomic-save/workspace validation, memory read-path allowlist policy, and the sectional TOML editor used by the Codex sync target.
